name: Jacqueline Clarke
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember waking up the first morning a ferry didn't run.” Friday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Jacqueline takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I complained about it last year. Now I need to tell the owner what I missed when it stopped.
appearance: Jacqueline has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Look for auburn hair cut square at the nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. In conversation Jacqueline raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Jacqueline never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Jacqueline can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To tell the owner why its silence mattered.
family: Anthony Penn is Jacqueline’s stepsibling. Jacqueline puts the kettle on. Anthony chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Anthony says, “I was too proud to sit with my former student.”
connections: Val Moss. A complaint about noise turns into an invitation for a more peaceful evening walk.

reactions.situation: The dock engine falls silent in mid-recording
reactions.response: Jacqueline notes the time the hum stopped before discussing a replacement recording.

reactions.response: Jacqueline asks for help with a task the neighbor does well, so both people get to contribute something.
